title: Introduction to Water
learningObjective: Students will identify the three states of water: solid, liquid, and gas
materials: Kettle or hot water (for steam demonstration)

procedure.instruction: Watch the video 'Water All Around Us' to learn about the three states of water.
scaffoldingSupports: Pause the video to discuss key points
Ask: 'Where do you see water at home?'

procedure.instruction: Look at pictures of ice, water, and steam. Sort them into three groups: solid, liquid, and gas.
scaffoldingSupports: Remind: Water you drink is liquid (pours)
Remind: Steam is water vapor - a gas you can't usually see

procedure.instruction: Complete the interactive activity: Sort images of water into solid, liquid, or gas.
scaffoldingSupports: Provide immediate feedback on each choice
Show real photos: ice cubes, water in glass, steam from kettle

procedure.instruction: Review vocabulary: solid, liquid, gas, water vapor.

multimediaResources.caption: Learn about the three states of water: solid, liquid, and gas
multimediaResources.accessibilityDescription: Video showing ice cubes melting into water, then water boiling into steam

multimediaResources.caption: Sort pictures into solid, liquid, or gas
multimediaResources.accessibilityDescription: Drag and drop activity with images of ice, water, and steam

exitTicket.questionText: Circle all the places where you see water:
exitTicket.correctAnswer: Ice cubes, Rain, Ocean, Steam from shower
exitTicket.explanation: Water can be found as ice, rain, in the ocean, and as steam! It's all around us in different forms.
